title: 2026-05-27-weekly-pilot-regression-and-quality-triage-with-blueharbor-shipping
next_steps: Redwood to share updated guardrail/scorecard spreadsheet by 2026-05-29
Customer to provide 1 week of new prompt logs for regression analysis by 2026-06-02
Schedule 2-hour load benchmark on Dedicated replica 2026-06-05
action_items: Maya Singh - rerun regression suite with pruned prompt set and attach results - due 2026-06-03
Carlos Mendez - send anonymized examples of failed cases and priority labels - due 2026-05-30
Jordan Li - share SOC2/ISO doc links and guardrail checklist - due 2026-05-29
summary: Weekly POC sync to triage recent regressions in scorecard, agree on prompt pruning, and plan targeted benchmarks. Identified two likely prompt patterns causing hallucinations and a scoring threshold issue; agreed on short-term fixes and measurement for next week.
topics: guardrail false positives vs recall tradeoff
questions: How much latency impact will autoscaling have on our tail p95?
Can the model fallback keep context with partial KV cache?
What level of audit log retention is included in Private deployment?
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly check-in for the BlueHarbor pilot. we've got about 45 minutes, agenda is quick triage of the new failures, prompt pruning plan, and next steps.
[00:18] Carlos Mendez: yeah thanks Ethan, um quick context - we saw a bump in the severity score yesterday, about 12% more high-severity flags, a lot of them around container delivery instructions being invented.
[00:32] Leah Tan: and to add, product's concerned because customers are seeing wrong port numbers, so it's customer-facing.
[00:40] Maya Singh: OK, quick note, we reran the scorecard against the batch from the 20th, and it's consistent, the false positive rate went up when the model temperature was bumped for throughput tests, so could be config drift.
[01:05] Omar Suleiman: we didn't intentionally change config in staging, but the SE pipeline did deploy a minor quantization profile - could that affect hallucination patterns?
[01:18] Maya Singh: yeah quantization can change decoding subtly, we often see n-gram hallucination shifts. also the runtime selected an alternative kernel for short sequences that might be less robust.
[01:33] Carlos Mendez: can you say that again - alternative what?
[01:36] Maya Singh: kernel, the GPU kernel; auto kernel selection swapped to a lower-precision path for peaks, um sometimes that gives different beams. transcription note: system said "kernal" earlier in logs.
[01:50] Ethan Park: right, so hypothesis one: kernel/quantization + temperature change. hypothesis two: prompt set contains ambiguous templates that amplify small model changes.
[02:05] Priya Rao: we pushed a new templated prompt last week to handle consolidated manifests, maybe that's the ambiguous template.
[02:12] Leah Tan: yep that was me, we wanted to reduce tokens.
[02:15] Maya Singh: token reduction can drop clarifying fields, so model fills in plausible defaults - port numbers etc.
[02:25] Carlos Mendez: we need to balance cost vs hallucination; Redwood's Optimize suggestions earlier said batching and prefix cache could help, is that still valid?
[02:35] Jordan Li: yes, there was a suggestion: increase prefix caching for static manifest header, that reduces new tokens per request and keeps context stable. we'll include config snippet in the doc.
[02:48] Ethan Park: on scoring, we noticed the threshold for the severity classifier is at 0.65, if we raise to 0.7 we catch fewer false positives but more false negatives; what do you prefer?
[03:05] Carlos Mendez: we'd rather reduce false negatives, security risk is higher.
[03:09] Leah Tan: but product needs lower noise for CS. maybe do per-route thresholds?
[03:15] Maya Singh: per-route thresholds are supported. we can do the manifest route at 0.72 and free-text at 0.65, and monitor.
[03:25] Ethan Park: quick note on guardrails: we saw a spike in guardrail rejects because a new extraction rule flagged measurement units. the rules were brittle.
[03:36] Priya Rao: those rules were regex-based, I can loosen them.
[03:40] Omar Suleiman: also on SSO and security, customer asked about KMS/HSM for Private - is that included?
[03:48] Jordan Li: yes, Private supports KMS integration and HSM options but we need to scope network egress for audit logs; I'll send the SOC2/ISO links.
[03:58] Carlos Mendez: perfect. um on benchmarks - we want a 2-hour dedicated run mirroring peak: 500 concurrent low-latency requests, can Redwood replicate that?
[04:10] Maya Singh: yes we can spin up a Dedicated replica with same quant/cluster; suggests running with the same token distribution, we'll coordinate a load window.
[04:20] Ethan Park: action items we'll capture, but before that, prompt pruning plan: Maya, propose algorithmic steps?
[04:28] Maya Singh: sure - one, create a subset of 2k prompts representing failures and pass cases; two, try synthetic counterfactuals swapping ports and addresses to test stability; three, prune ambiguous templates and run A/B in pilot for 48 hours. I'll attach the pruning script.
[04:45] Priya Rao: where do we put the logs? we can't share PII, will anonymize.
[04:50] Carlos Mendez: we'll mask personally identifiable numbers, yes.
[04:55] Leah Tan: can Redwood run the regression locally against our masked logs?
[04:58] Maya Singh: yes, either we run in your VPC with Private deployment or you share masked logs and we run in hosted sandbox under NDA.
[05:08] Omar Suleiman: prefer VPC run.
[05:10] Ethan Park: noted. now any blockers from legal/procurement?
[05:15] Carlos Mendez: procurement asked for deletion SLA for logs, and clarity on data residency - EU vs US.
[05:22] Jordan Li: Private deployments can be region-locked; deletion SLA we can propose 30 days for logs with custom retention on enterprise plan. I'll follow up with the exact matrix.
[05:33] Ethan Park: ok let's recap.
[05:35] Ethan Park: recap: Maya to run pruning and regression, Carlos to send masked failed examples, Jordan to send SOC2/ISO + retention matrix, Redwood to schedule dedicated 2-hour benchmark.
[05:45] Carlos Mendez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:48] Leah Tan: thanks, we'll aim to have the log bundle by Friday.
[05:52] Ethan Park: great, end of call.
